newsitem.title: UK: UK shippers to help airlines with cargo forecasts.
newsitem.headline: UK shippers to help airlines with cargo forecasts.

text.p: Britain's Freight Transport Association said it is to survey its shipper members to assist the air cargo industry with more accurate airfreight traffic forecasting than is currently available.
It said it had made this commitment at the request of the UK Air Freight Forum, formed in November 1996 and comprising 20 leading airlines, freight forwarders and shippers.

The FTA said the aim was to prepare short-, medium-, and long-term traffic forecasts, measured in tonnes, in the areas of: Type of cargo; time-definite versus flight specific; and region-to-region (specifying routes where possible).
The FTA's shipping and air manager Andrew Traill said a trial survey of a limited number of members would initially be undertaken, to be followed by a survey of its 'top 100' shipper members.
"It will be difficult to obtain all the information needed but we hope to publish the results of the full survey in the spring of next year," he said.
"We hope it will lead to tangible benefits for all involved in the UK air cargo industry," Traill added.
